_schema.about: Registry of every flagged FEATURE and every dev SCREEN. Backward compatible: the server still reads flags.<key>.dev / .prod, and the app still turns each ON flag into a body class ff-<key>. Everything else here is descriptive metadata rendered by the Dev Area hub.

fields.label: Human name shown in the hub / Release Center.
fields.description: What it actually is, in one line.
fields.added: YYYY-MM-DD the thing first landed in the repo (from AGENT_UPDATE_LOG.md). 'unknown' if genuinely not recorded.
fields.updated: optional YYYY-MM-DD of the last material revision.
fields.status: live (real + working) | preview (works but honestly labelled, not backed by real data/algorithm) | placeholder (illustrative only)
fields.where: { screen, spot, file } — the precise place this lives.
fields.destination: screens only — where the screen lands in the product when its flag is ON. Lior's decision, per screen.
fields.url: screens only — the path the screen is served at.
fields.dev: boolean — ON in the dev environment.

_schema.last_updated: 2026-10-28 UTC · Full-Stack · add opt-in user testing flag; preserve every existing switch.

new_logo.label: New logo
new_logo.description: Updated GFI / MeatCODE logo in the top bar.

where.spot: Top bar, far left — the MeatCODE wordmark (.brand-name); adds a 'new' pill after it until the real asset is dropped in.

new_logo.note: Fixed 2026-08-15 (Coordinator): the mockup's CSS said body.ff-new-logo (hyphen) while the flag emits body.ff-new_logo (underscore), so the switch did nothing. Selectors realigned to the flag key — the toggle now works. Still a placeholder treatment until the real logo asset is dropped in.

dev_banner.label: Dev banner
dev_banner.description: Show a 'DEV · staging' ribbon so you never mistake staging for production.

where.spot: Was a fixed ribbon pinned to the top-centre of the viewport, above the top bar (#ffDevBanner).

dev_banner.note: 2026-08-16: the #ffDevBanner element + its CSS were removed from app/meatcode_mockup.html at Lior's request, so this flag is now INERT (nothing renders even when ON). Retire this entry, or re-add the ribbon element if the staging-vs-prod visual signal is wanted back.

inventory.label: Inventory button
inventory.description: Show the Inventory saved-items button and allow its drawer to open. Hiding it preserves saved items; this is a UI control, not an authorization boundary.

where.spot: Top bar Inventory button and saved-items drawer.

highlight_inventory.label: Highlight Inventory
highlight_inventory.description: Give the Inventory button a colored glow to draw attention to it.

where.spot: Top bar, right cluster — the Inventory / Toolbench button (.mc-toolbench-btn) gains a brass ring.

dev_area.label: Dev Area
dev_area.description: Show the Dev Area button (internal workbench: registry, WIP screens, docs, screen flows). Keep OFF in prod permanently.

where.spot: Top bar, immediately right of the Inventory button — the flask link (.mc-devarea-btn) to /app/dev/index.html.

dev_area.note: Never promote to prod. Individual screens graduate by getting their own flag flipped, not by shipping the Dev Area.

backup_center.label: Backups button
backup_center.description: Topbar button + dropdown letting anyone with the site password download a repo backup (GET /api/backup) or the actual Neon data (GET /api/data-backup) with one click — for Daniel/Yochai, no raw API URLs to remember.

where.spot: Top bar, immediately right of the Dev Area button — .mc-backup-wrap / .mc-backup-btn.

backup_center.note: Set dev:true / prod:false deliberately, same as Dev Area — Lior asked for this to be reachable on staging only for now. To ship it to prod: flip this flag's prod to true here (or in the Release Center admin page), then run promote-to-prod.command. The two download endpoints stay behind the normal site password either way — the flag only controls whether the BUTTON is visible, not whether the endpoints respond.

papers_browser.label: Papers browser
papers_browser.description: Dev-team module: browse every paper in Neon (sources) with filters/sort, 50 per page, tick rows to export CSV/XLSX, export the whole table as CSV, open each paper's link / best-effort open-access PDF.

where.screen: Top nav chip 'Papers' + in-app #papers scene (iframes app/dev/papers_browser.html?embed=1)
where.spot: Top-nav chip + backend routes /api/papers-browser/* (flag OFF → 404)

papers_browser.note: Dev-only on purpose (dev:true / prod:false). Backend routes 404 when the flag is off for the environment, so prod exposes nothing until Lior flips prod:true and runs promote-to-prod.command.

maillard_sim.label: Maillard simulator
maillard_sim.description: Show the Simulate module and enable its simulator API. Off hides navigation, starter actions and direct scene links.

where.screen: API only — no UI wired yet
where.spot: Platform navigation, simulator starter and /api/simulate routes

maillard_sim.note: Runs in MAILLARD_MODE=mock by default — deterministic SYNTHETIC output, every response marked "mode":"mock" and synthetic:true. The real simulator is a Docker prototype and a Render runtime:python service cannot spawn Docker, so production needs the separate runtime:docker service commented into render.yaml (then MAILLARD_MODE=http). Keep prod false until that service exists.

knowledge_graph.label: Knowledge Graph explorer
knowledge_graph.description: Literature/molecule knowledge-graph explorer, embedded from the standalone KG explorer artifact.

where.spot: 'Knowledge Graph' card; the page itself is a full-height iframe of /kg/kg_explorer.html with a fallback message.

knowledge_graph.destination: Dev Area only — direction still open in platform_docs/KG_DECISION.md (bridge density is the blocker).

fingerprint.label: Meat Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: 8-axis aroma radar of a sample vs a reference (beef sirloin demo vs dashed plant analog).

where.spot: 'Meat Fingerprint' card; the page carries a PLACEHOLDER banner above the canvas radar.

fingerprint.destination: Dev Area only for now — proposed landing is a Research tile (MVP board A1); blocked until the fingerprint schema is defined. Lior's call.

analytics.label: Analytics zone
analytics.description: Show Analytics in the platform navigation and the analytical-methods overview. The workspace is a preview using illustrative data; GC-MS literature data is available in the Meaty Volatile Library.

where.screen: Platform top navigation → Analytics; Dev Area → Screens
where.spot: Analytics navigation opens the in-app workspace. The Dev Area card opens the methods overview.

analytics.destination: Platform navigation → Analytics workspace (preview). This canonical switch takes precedence over the legacy analytics_module setting.

compare.label: Compare screen
compare.description: Side-by-side molecule comparison (2-AP vs methional grid, diff chips, add a third column) — the Flow 2 target.

where.spot: 'Compare screen' card; the page opens with the Flow-2 carry banner naming the entities handed over.

compare.destination: Oracle answer → 'Compare these two →' handoff (screen-flow Flow 2). Ships behind this flag once the handoff bus lands.

versions.label: Production version history
versions.description: Every promoted prod snapshot, newest-first, with the live one marked and a per-snapshot re-migrate button.

where.spot: 'Production version history' card; the page reads GET /api/release/history (visible on hosted dev, rollback POST stays local-admin).

versions.destination: Dev Area only — release machinery is internal and rollback runs from the Mac.

oracle_redesign.label: Oracle redesign (v11 chat)
oracle_redesign.description: Proposed next Oracle: multi-turn chat thread, approved answer-card anatomy, attach + dictate in the ask box, history rail unchanged.

where.spot: 'Oracle redesign' card; the page is a static design artifact — Ask honestly says retrieval is not wired.

oracle_redesign.destination: Dev Area only — approved patterns get ported into app/meatcode_mockup.html; the thread itself needs multi-turn retrieval before it graduates.

analytics_workspace.label: Analytics workspace (bring-your-own data)
analytics_workspace.description: List the guided GC-MS / NMR workspace preview in the Dev Area. This switch does not control the platform's Analytics navigation; use Analytics zone for that. Comparisons currently use illustrative data.

where.spot: 'Analytics workspace' card; the page carries a PREVIEW banner - guided stepper on illustrative data, no real parsing.

analytics_workspace.destination: Dev Area listing only. The platform Analytics entry is controlled by analytics. The legacy analytics_module switch is a fallback only when analytics is absent.
analytics_workspace.note: Guided-stepper mockup (method -> upload -> confirm format -> reference -> compare). Figures are generated for demonstration; wiring to real /api/* + a reference-profile source (A1/A3) is the follow-up.

research_reaction_network.label: Research - reaction network journey
research_reaction_network.description: New Research journey: pick lipid or aqueous precursors -> curated Heat+Reaction Network (precursors -> reactions -> volatiles) enriched with real Neon volatiles -> inline analytical + sensory profiles that link to the analytics workspace.

where.spot: 'Research - reaction network journey' card; PREVIEW banner - curated skeleton, real volatiles where backed.

research_reaction_network.destination: LIVE INTEGRATION (2026-09-01): gates the #research scene in app/meatcode_mockup.html - when ff-research_reaction_network is ON, Research shows this wizard iframed (embed mode); OFF keeps the old phase-picker. Flip prod + promote-to-prod to graduate.
research_reaction_network.note: UI consumes GET /api/reaction-network?branch=lipid|aqueous (real volatiles from meaty_volatile_library; precursors/reactions/edges are curated skeleton). Distinct from Simulate. Endpoint 404s until deploy-dev -> UI runs on embedded demo until then.

analytics_module.label: Analytics module (legacy navigation switch)
analytics_module.description: Compatibility fallback for installations without an Analytics zone setting. Ignored when Analytics zone exists; use Analytics zone to show or hide the navigation entry.

where.spot: Top bar, before Simulate; analytics controls visibility. analytics_module is read only if the canonical analytics key is absent.

analytics_module.destination: Platform navigation → in-app Analytics workspace preview. /analytics remains a secondary direct entry.
analytics_module.note: Legacy fallback only: an explicit analytics true or false takes precedence. analytics_workspace only controls its Dev Area listing. Saved local switches reach production after promotion and successful deployment.

science_module.label: Science module (top nav)
science_module.description: MeatCODE Science: guided Foundations tour (raw -> cooked meat) + Precursors (juice, fat, meat matrix) with illustrative example studies; every 'Ask' hands off to the real Oracle and 'Experts' to the Ecosystem.

where.screen: Top nav (all topbars), 2nd chip right after Oracle
where.spot: Chip 'Science' -> in-app #science scene iframing /app/modules/science.html?embed=1 (full-width, no context panel).

science_module.destination: Top-nav 'Science' (Yochai, 2026-10-25). Ported from the 'MeatCODE Science Mockup' Chat artifact (v0.2, 18 Oct) onto the live platform tokens.
science_module.note: Static, pre-generated content (per the Science brief). Example-study cards are labelled Illustrative; the flavor-benchmark panel is held back until the TVP rationale exists. Process-flavor path is 'Coming soon'. PROMOTED 2026-10-25: prod ON after Yochai's staging check.

ecosystem_module.label: Ecosystem module (top nav)
ecosystem_module.description: MeatCODE Ecosystem: intent-first expert directory (People) + Radar of approved events/courses/news; public-information-only expert cards with 'Ask GFI for an introduction'; hands off to the Oracle and Science.

where.screen: Top nav (all topbars), chip right after Science
where.spot: Chip 'Ecosystem' -> in-app #ecosystem scene iframing /app/modules/ecosystem.html?embed=1 (full-width, no context panel).

ecosystem_module.destination: Top-nav 'Ecosystem' (Yochai, 2026-10-25). Ported from 'MeatCODE Ecosystem prototype v0.8' (Chat artifact, 13 Oct) incl. Lior's 11 Oct review notes.
ecosystem_module.note: People + papers LIVE from Neon (GET /api/ecosystem/people, SELECT-only, 10-min cache; 155 people / 109 papers on 25 Oct = the 8 Oct snapshot's 153/108 + 2 accented names it had missed). The bundled 8 Oct copy in ecosystem_data.json is only a labelled fallback when Neon is unreachable. Radar = human-reviewed Agent Inbox rows only. Privacy per the 14 Oct decision: no emails, no relevance score/tier, correction/removal link on every card. PROMOTED 2026-10-25: prod ON after Yochai's staging check.

oracle_guided.label: Guided Oracle (elicitation questions)
oracle_guided.description: The Oracle asks up to 3 short clarifying questions (one per turn, with typical values to tap, 'Just answer' always available) before answering formulation-type questions; answers open with a 'Working from:' line and end with 'Open in Science' / 'Experts on this'.

where.spot: askOracle() sends {guided:true, history} to POST /api/ask; the server's elicitation step may reply with an `ask` SSE event (question + options) instead of an answer.

oracle_guided.note: Implements the Oracle elicitation spec (closed 11 Oct). Flag OFF -> /api/ask behaves exactly as before (single-turn, no questions). Retrieval and citations are the existing grounded pipeline, unchanged. PROMOTED 2026-10-25: prod ON after Yochai's staging check.

research_nav_hidden.label: Hide Research tab (Science replaces it)
research_nav_hidden.description: Science takes Research's place in the top nav: the Research chip is hidden in every topbar while science_module is also on. Hidden, not deleted — the #research scene, its wizard and every in-content link into it (e.g. Science's 'Molecular map' card) keep working.

where.spot: The static 'Research' chip gets class .mc-nav-hidden (display:none) from the product-modules chip pass; turning either flag off brings it back.

research_nav_hidden.note: Yochai, 26 Oct: "Science module replaces Research (hide, don't delete)". Requires science_module ON as well, so the nav can never lose both.

user_testing.label: User testing and feedback
user_testing.description: Opt-in Microsoft Clarity session research and isolated anonymous feedback; no capture before consent.

where.spot: Research consent and feedback controls; authenticated /api/research/* routes.

user_testing.note: Requires the isolated user_research database schema. USER_RESEARCH_ENABLED=false is an emergency capture switch; withdrawal stays available. Clarity loads only after explicit consent.

live_testing_dashboard.label: Live testing dashboard
live_testing_dashboard.description: Private production journey inputs, module clicks, consented chats and read-only troubleshooting from the development server.

where.spot: Research operations

live_testing_dashboard.note: Requires separate research-admin credential. Production reads use a SELECT-only research database role; no shell or deployment commands.
